description: Hook points every kernel station fires (the kernel and kernel_llm programs): before_verdict, after_verdict, before_reply. The canonical copy is in the kernel program's folder; each kernel definition folder carries one (kernel_hooks.json, named by "hooks" at the top of its interfaces.json), with the four aos-loop points added by a directive when the kernel runs under aos-loop. The kernel's own rules (in its code, tools/aos/kernel/hooks.py; this file only tells): exit 10 blocks (all three points); exit 0 with a JSON object on stdout replaces the keys of output; after_verdict's condition is compared with verdict; a failing hook stops the round (HookFailed).

before_verdict.description: a new request letter is about to be judged by the built-in rules (letters already in the queue do not pass here again)

stack.description: the kernel's stack (the handler's own AOS_STACK is STACK/hookeds/NAME/)

output.description: exit 0 with a JSON object on stdout: these keys replace the event's

before_verdict.if_blocked: the letter is refused (HookRejected, or BudgetMissing when the hook's stdout says so); the built-in rules and after_verdict do not run

after_verdict.description: the station judged a new letter, or a queued letter leaves the queue; fired hook by hook

stack.description: the kernel's stack (the handler's own AOS_STACK is STACK/hookeds/NAME/)

verdict.description: the verdict so far: pass, refuse or queue from the rules (an earlier hook may have changed it, also to hold)

decision.description: stations that can hold only: pass when someone already said so, else null

next.description: stations that forward only: null (the hook may give the next mailbox)

output.description: exit 0 with a JSON object on stdout: these keys replace the event's

after_verdict.subject: verdict
after_verdict.if_blocked: the letter is refused (HookRejected, or BudgetMissing when the hook's stdout says so)

before_reply.description: a reply passes this station on its way back (only with reply_via_me)

stack.description: the kernel's stack (the handler's own AOS_STACK is STACK/hookeds/NAME/)

output.description: exit 0 with a JSON object on stdout: these keys replace the event's

before_reply.if_blocked: the reply is not applied: {"applied": false, "error": {"code": "HookRejected", ...}} goes back instead
